exposure: psychological factors (depression, psychotropic drug intake, psychotherapy)
outcome: long-term success of therapeutic local anesthesia (TLA)
therapy response (NAS <= 4 for at least 6 months)
cohort: The study re-evaluated 45 patients diagnosed with severe chronic vulvodynia or chronic vulvar pain (NAS >= 6, duration >= 6 months) who had previously been treated with TLA.
finding: The study demonstrates the long-term effectiveness of therapeutic local anesthesia (TLA) in women with vulvodynia, supporting the hypothesis that neuralgia of one or more nerves of the pelvic floor is an important component in the development of the condition.
mod_finding: The number of deliveries and cesarean sections had no impact on the long-term success of therapeutic local anesthesia for vulvodynia.
followup_time: 7.9 years (range 4.5-13 years) after the end of therapy
